content_units: First 90 Minutes Dancefloor Plan

Mixed-age crowd,  80 guests, with a gentle start, steady lift, and broad genre spread. This sequence stays clean-friendly, uses familiar singalongs early, adds funk/disco/pop/rock/R&B/country touches, and includes well over 4 songs from the 1980s/1990s.
20-Song Open Dancing Sequence
Song   Artist   Era   Vibe   Transition note
1   Signed, Sealed, Delivered (I'm Yours)   Stevie Wonder   1970s   Warm, welcoming   Opens with instant recognition and a friendly groove so older and younger guests feel comfortable stepping in.
2   I Wanna Dance with Somebody   Whitney Houston   1980s   Bright pop lift   Keeps the floor safe and familiar while raising energy with a bigger chorus and more obvious dance pulse.
3   September   Earth, Wind & Fire   1970s   Funky, joyful   Moves from pop into timeless party funk, widening age appeal without changing the mood too sharply.
4   Man! I Feel Like a Woman!   Shania Twain   1990s   Country-pop fun   Introduces a genre shift to keep things from feeling one-note while preserving singalong confidence.
5   Billie Jean   Michael Jackson   1980s   Cool groove   Pulls the room back into an irresistible beat after the country-pop spike, keeping dancers locked in.
6   Shut Up and Dance   WALK THE MOON   2010s   Upbeat pop-rock   Takes the recognizable groove of "Billie Jean" and converts it into a more modern, jumping energy.
7   Dancing Queen   ABBA   1970s   Cross-generational classic   Slightly eases the intensity while boosting singalong value so more casual dancers rejoin.
8   This Is How We Do It   Montell Jordan   1990s   Laid-back party R&B   Swings into a bouncier hip-hop/R&B pocket to refresh the room before the next climb.
9   Uptown Funk   Mark Ronson ft. Bruno Mars   2010s   Big funk-pop peak   Builds directly from the bounce of the previous track into a louder, brassier floor-filler.
10   Twist and Shout   The Beatles   1960s   Rock-and-roll burst   Uses the peak to bring in older guests with a universally known shout-along and simple dance feel.
11   Levitating   Dua Lipa   2020s   Disco-pop glide   Modernizes the floor again with a sleek beat that keeps momentum without sounding harsh.
12   Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'   Michael Jackson   1980s   Percussive drive   Extends the dance groove and raises urgency with layered rhythm and nonstop motion.
13   Everybody (Backstreet's Back)   Backstreet Boys   1990s   Nostalgic pop explosion   Turns rhythmic momentum into a millennial singalong moment that still lands for mixed ages.
14   Yeah!   Usher ft. Lil Jon & Ludacris   2000s   High-energy club   Pushes into a stronger late-set gear once the room has fully committed to dancing.
15   Footloose   Kenny Loggins   1980s   Fast, playful   Keeps the pace high but shifts from club to feel-good rock-pop to avoid genre fatigue.
16   Mr. Brightside   The Killers   2000s   Indie-rock singalong   Leans into shout-singing energy, great once the crowd is loosened up and fully engaged.
17   Yeah 3x   Chris Brown   2010s   Hands-up pop   Smoothly pivots from rock-singalong into a clean, festival-like pulse for another burst upward.
18   Don't Stop Believin'   Journey   1980s   Anthem reset   Briefly trades pure dancing for a unifying singalong moment that keeps the room emotionally high.
19   Can't Stop the Feeling!   Justin Timberlake   2010s   Happy pop release   Converts the anthem moment back into easy dance movement, ideal for bringing everyone in again.
20   Crazy in Love   Beyoncé ft. Jay-Z   2000s   Confident closer for segment   Ends the 90-minute arc with a strong, celebratory beat that sets up the next dance block perfectly.
Crowd-Flow Notes
-   Songs 1-4:   Safe, familiar, low-pressure entry.
-   Songs 5-9:   Noticeable build into the first true peak.
-   Songs 10-13:   Variety pocket to keep all age groups invested.
-   Songs 14-17:   Highest sustained dance energy of the set.
-   Songs 18-20:   Big communal singalong, then re-entry into dance-floor momentum.
DJ Read on Why This Works
Option 1: Balanced mixed-age arc   Familiar early, modern later, multiple genres represented   Best overall wedding-safe choice
Option 2: Strong nostalgia coverage   Heavy 80s/90s anchors keep broad appeal   Great for family-heavy receptions
Option 3: Flexible energy control   Easy to shorten or extend around songs 8, 13, or 18   Useful if speeches or photo moments shift timing
